question: For $$M=\begin{bmatrix}a & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & a & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & a\end{bmatrix},$$ examine the type of matrix obtained in each case: (i) $a=0$, (ii) $a=1$, (iii) $a\neq0,1$. State all applicable types among square, diagonal, scalar, zero and identity matrices.
explanation:
Common structure
For every value of $a$, $M$ is a $3\times3$ square matrix with all off-diagonal entries zero and all diagonal entries equal. Hence, it is always a diagonal matrix and a scalar matrix.
Case $a=0$
$$M=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus, $M$ is a zero matrix; it is also square, diagonal and scalar.
Case $a=1$
$$M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}=I_3$$
Thus, $M$ is an identity matrix; it is also square, diagonal and scalar.
Case $a\neq0,1$
$M$ is a non-zero scalar matrix and hence is also diagonal and square, but it is neither the zero matrix nor the identity matrix.

options.A: (i) square and zero only; (ii) identity only; (iii) diagonal only
options.B: (i) square, diagonal and zero; (ii) square, diagonal and identity; (iii) square and diagonal
options.C: (i) scalar and identity; (ii) zero and scalar; (iii) identity and diagonal
options.D: (i) square, diagonal, scalar and zero; (ii) square, diagonal, scalar and identity; (iii) square, diagonal and scalar
